title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 1st District
area: Bucks County and part of Montgomery County, in the Philadelphia suburbs.

context.text: Brian Fitzpatrick won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary unopposed. Bob Harvie won the Democratic primary, defeating Lucia Simonelli.

summary.text: Brian Fitzpatrick is the Republican incumbent, a former FBI special agent and federal prosecutor first elected to Congress in 2016 to succeed his brother Michael Fitzpatrick. He serves on the Ways and Means Committee and the House Intelligence Committee, where he chairs a subcommittee, and co-chairs the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus.

background.text: According to his official biography, he was born and raised in Levittown, in Pennsylvania's 1st Congressional District, and graduated from Bishop Egan High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Penn State University and a law degree from the Dickinson School of Law; his official biography says he holds a JD and MBA from Penn State through a joint degree program.

Spent 15 years as an FBI special agent and federal prosecutor, including work as a supervisory special agent and special assistant United States attorney; his official biography says he was embedded with U.S. Special Forces during Operation Iraqi Freedom and served as national supervisor in the FBI's Public Corruption Unit.

His official biography lists FBI honors including the FBI Director's Award and Investigator of the Year for his role as lead case agent in Operation City Lights, a public-corruption investigation in New York City.
Is a licensed attorney, certified public accountant and certified emergency medical technician.

Won the 2016 general election for Pennsylvania's 8th Congressional District with 54.4% of the vote over Democratic state Rep. Steve Santarsiero, succeeding his older brother Michael G. Fitzpatrick, who did not seek re-election; the district is now numbered the 1st.

Serves on the Ways and Means Committee (Health and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees) and on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, where his official page lists him as a subcommittee chairman, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Co-chairs the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus and, according to his official biography, co-chairs nearly 20 caucuses and task forces and has been designated by House leadership as a Congressional Representative to NATO.
Advanced unopposed from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, receiving 44,365 votes.

record.text: Introduced a bipartisan measure to bar members of Congress from profiting off earmarks (announced September 17, 2026).
Led a bipartisan effort to shield ratepayers from data center costs that passed the House (announced September 16, 2026).
Helped secure final passage of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (announced September 16, 2026).

candidates.name: Bob Harvie
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating Lucia Simonelli.
candidates.currentRole: Chair, Bucks County Board of Commissioners

summary.text: Bob Harvie is the Democratic nominee and chair of the Bucks County Board of Commissioners. A former high school social studies teacher, he served on the Falls Township Board of Supervisors from 2003 and was elected county commissioner in 2019 and re-elected in 2023. He won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary, and his campaign says he is running to fight for middle-class and working families.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was born and raised in Bristol Borough and is a lifelong Bucks County resident; he graduated from Bristol High School.
Graduated magna cum laude from George Washington University with a bachelor's degree in history and holds a master's degree in education from Holy Family University.

Taught high school social studies for 26 years, including 20 years as a teacher and social studies department chairman at Bucks County Technical High School, where he started the Beyond the Books program bringing military veterans into classrooms.

After moving to Falls Township in 1999, served two years on the township Planning Commission and was elected to the Falls Township Board of Supervisors in 2003; he chaired the board from 2008 to 2020.
Elected to the Bucks County Board of Commissioners in November 2019 and sworn in January 6, 2020; re-elected to a second term in November 2023.
Named chair of the Board of Commissioners on January 5, 2022, and named vice chair and then chair again at the January 2025 reorganization.
Defeated Lucia Simonelli, 65.1% to 34.9%, in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for Pennsylvania's 1st District.

priorities.text: Wants to permanently restore and expand Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, lower the Medicare buy-in age from 65 to 55, and let Medicare negotiate prescription drug prices and cap insulin costs.
Supports a middle-class tax cut while ensuring large corporations and the ultra-wealthy "pay their fair share."
Wants to roll back tariffs he says raise consumer prices and raise the federal minimum wage to $15 per hour.
Supports overturning Citizens United, banning corporate PAC contributions, banning congressional stock trading, and a lifetime lobbying ban for former members of Congress.

positions.summary: Supports permanently restoring ACA premium tax credits, lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 55, and letting Medicare negotiate drug prices.
positions.quote: I'll fight to permanently restore and expand those tax credits so families don't wake up to hundreds of dollars in higher monthly premiums simply because Congress failed to act. I believe we need to lower the age that Americans can buy into Medicare from 65 to 55.

positions.summary: Supports a middle-class tax cut paid for by ensuring large corporations and the ultra-wealthy pay a higher share.
positions.quote: I'll fight for a middle class tax cut while ensuring large corporations and the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share so middle class Americans get a much needed tax cut.

positions.summary: Supports raising the federal minimum wage to $15 per hour.
positions.quote: For too long, the minimum wage in this country has remained stagnant. I believe we need to raise the minimum wage to $15 per hour.

positions.summary: Opposes the tariffs enacted under the Trump administration, saying they raise costs for food and household goods.
positions.quote: I will fight to roll back Trump's tariffs that unnecessarily increase the cost of food and household essentials for American consumers.

positions.summary: Supports expanding clean energy and modernizing the electric grid, and criticized the 2025 reconciliation law for cutting clean-energy tax credits.
positions.quote: That's why I'll fight to expand clean energy, modernize our electric grid, and build resilient roads, bridges, and public transit systems that keep our economy moving.
